entries.title: Elektrische Bahn Lana–Meran
text: A poster for the electric railway from Lana to Merano by Anton Reckziegel, 1906: a painted river valley with a castle on a cliff. Kept as a point of comparison from before the war, when the province was Austrian. The copy carries a dealer's watermark.
facts: Habsburg-era comparison: poster 'Elektrische Bahn Lana–Meran' by Anton Reckziegel, 1906 (manifest)
Commons gives its source as artifiche.com (manifest)
One of the two Habsburg-era comparison posters among the openly licensed images (notes 01, Q1 §E)

Seen in the image: a painted view down a river valley, a castle on a cliff at left, a town on both banks of the river and mountains behind; 'Elektrische Bahn Lana-Meran' and 'Kunstanstalt Müller & Zürich' at the foot; an 'Artifiche – Swiss Poster Gallery' watermark across the picture

images.caption: Anton Reckziegel, 1906. Public domain. Wikimedia Commons (from artifiche.com).

entries.title: Gruss aus der Elektrischen Schwebebahn von Bozen (265 m.) nach Kohlern (1140 m.)
text: A print for the cable car from Bozen up to Kohlern, about 1908–10, photographed where it hangs in the Zeughaus in Innsbruck: a cabin with curtained windows and passengers above a ridge. The second pre-war comparison piece.
The manifest calls it a poster. Its heading, “Gruss aus …”, is the formula of a picture postcard.
facts: Habsburg-era comparison: photo (2020) of the poster for the Kohlerer Bahn (Funivia del Colle), Bozen, c. 1908–10, on display at the Zeughaus Innsbruck; poster anonymous (manifest)
One of the two Habsburg-era comparison posters among the openly licensed images (notes 01, Q1 §E)

Seen in the image: a sepia print photographed against a grey wall: a cable-car cabin with curtained, latticed windows and passengers, hanging from cables above a mountain ridge; heading 'Gruss aus der Elektrischen Schwebebahn von Bozen (265 m.) nach Kohlern (1140 m.)'
Doubt: the 'Gruss aus …' greeting heading is the formula of a picture postcard; the manifest and the Commons file name call the object a poster (image vs manifest)

images.caption: Anonymous, c. 1908–10; photo by Asurnipal, 2020, at the Zeughaus Innsbruck. CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons.

entries.creator: Anonymous; photo: Asurnipal

confidence.note: the manifest calls it a poster; its 'Gruss aus' heading reads like a postcard

entries.title: Bozner Nachrichten, 20 April 1921: advertisement for the Bozner Messe
text: A newspaper advertisement for the Bolzano fair of 19 to 26 April 1921, signed by the association “Bozner Messe”: exhibitions, concerts on the Waltherplatz, a procession in traditional dress, special trains from Franzensfeste, Trento and Merano.
The fair's own poster of that year is the only fair poster of the period. It was not downloaded, being in copyright until 2033. No inter-war poster for a “Fiera di Bolzano” was found.
facts: Newspaper advertisement for the Bozner Messe (Bolzano fair), Bozner Nachrichten, 20 April 1921; crop from digital.tessmann.it (manifest)
The 1921 Bozner Messe is the only fair poster of the period; no interwar poster for a 'Fiera di Bolzano' was found, and the Salce fair posters date from 1951 on (notes 01, Q1)
The Bozner Messe poster itself (Otto Zoff, 1921, PMM 11334) was not downloaded: Zoff died 1963, so in the EU it is in copyright until 2033 (manifest; notes 01, Q1 #3, [DB✓])

Seen in the image: a bordered advertisement headed 'BOZNER MESSE (19.–26. April 1921.)' beside a 'BM' emblem; it lists exhibitions in the Messe-Palast, Freiturnplatz, Museum and Bürgersaal, concerts on the Waltherplatz, a 'Südtiroler Trachtenzug' on Sunday 24 April and 'Messe-Züge' from Franzensfeste, Trient and Meran, and is signed 'Verein „Bozner Messe“'

images.caption: Bozner Nachrichten, 20 April 1921. CC BY-SA 4.0, crop from digital.tessmann.it via Wikimedia Commons.

entries.title: Municipio di Bolzano – Cittadini! / Bürger!
text: A bilingual notice from the town hall of Bolzano, 19 May 1925, signed by the prefectural commissioner Steffanini. It orders every house on the route of a visit by Italian war invalids to fly the tricolour, and calls Bolzano “die Königin des Hochetsch”, the official German for Alto Adige. The territory, in the research's translation, is “designated as ours by natural borders and history”.
In the photograph only the German column is whole. The Italian one is cut off at the edge.
facts: Photo (2020) of a bilingual municipal public notice 'Municipio di Bolzano – Cittadini! / Bürger!', 19 May 1925, signed by Prefectural Commissioner Steffanini; it orders tricolour flags for the visit of Italian war invalids; at the left edge, part of a Fränzl-printed tourist poster (manifest)

A civic propaganda poster: it orders every house on the invalids' route to fly a tricolour and calls Bolzano 'die Königin des Hochetsch', the German official rendering of 'Alto Adige' (notes 01, Q4, [IMG✓])
The territory is 'designated as ours by natural borders and history … sealed by the long sacrifices and shining victories of our legions' (notes 01, Q4, [IMG✓])

Seen in the image: the notice on a pale wall inside a border of red fruit and green leaves; only the German column is whole ('Bürger!', 'Vom Rathause Bolzano, 19. Mai 1925', 'Der Präfekturskommissär STEFFANINI'); the Italian column is cut off at the left edge, where part of a blue-framed tourist poster shows

entries.title: Bolzano: Ferrovia del Renon e S. Maddalena verso la Mendola

entries.title: Dolomiten, 27 June 1932, page 8: advertisement for La Rinascente
text: An advertisement in the Catholic German-language daily Dolomiten for a clearance sale at La Rinascente, the Italian department store in Bolzano: “10.000 Paar Herren-, Damen- u. Kinder-Schuhe zum Selbstkosten-Preis”. An Italian chain sells to German-speaking readers in their own language, under a running head set in Fraktur.
facts: German-language ad for the Italian department store 'La Rinascente' (Bolzano), in the Catholic-German daily Dolomiten, 27 June 1932 (manifest)

entries.title: Oltrisarco, postcard with its German caption struck out
text: A coloured postcard of the Oltrisarco housing district from 1933. The German place name in the caption has been covered with a black bar and “Oltrisarco” printed beside it. It is the Italianization of place names made visible: a correction applied to a card that already existed.
facts: Coloured postcard of the Oltrisarco/Oberau housing district: the German place name is struck through with black bars and 'Oltrisarco' is overprinted, a visible trace of toponymic Italianisation (manifest)
Cited as Italianisation recorded physically on the card, beside Amonn cards whose German names were overstamped with Italian ones (notes 01, Q5, [IMG✓])
Publisher unknown; scan by Flickr user 'paolo from tv' (manifest)

Seen in the image: a hand-coloured bird's-eye view of a block of three- and four-storey houses with red roofs among green fields, a river and the town across it, mountains behind; at top left an italic caption is covered by a black bar and 'Oltrisarco' is printed in bold beside it

images.caption: Unknown publisher, 1933; scan by 'paolo from tv' (Flickr). Public domain (PD-Italy). Wikimedia Commons.

entries.rights: Public domain (PD-Italy 20 years; PD US no notice)

entries.title: Merano
text: Franz Lenhart's poster for Merano, published by the state tourist board ENIT in 1934: a woman's tanned face in a cone of light, palm fronds, a white mountain over the town. No traditional dress and no monument. The regime is present only in the two emblems at the foot, ENIT's and the state railways'.
This copy is the Hungarian National Museum's. The artwork is in copyright until 2062.
facts: ENIT poster 'MERANO': woman's head in a beam of light, palm fronds, Merano townscape; ENIT and FS crowned-wreath logos; matches Touriseum inv. 4070493 (1934, Off. Grafiche Coen & C., Milano) (manifest)
The Touriseum record names ENIT as publisher ('Herausgeber'); this copy is the Hungarian National Museum's (notes 01, Q1 #23, [DB✓], [IMG✓])
A modern female head in a cone of light, with no Tracht (notes 01, Q4, [IMG✓])
The regime enters the tourist posters through logos, ENIT and FS with the Savoy crown, rather than through monuments (notes 01, Q4)
Rights: the artwork is in copyright until 2062 (Lenhart died 1992), so non-commercial academic use only, with attribution (manifest)
Lenhart's dates conflict between sources: 1898–1992 in the OMA authority record, 1892–1992 at the Hungarian National Museum (notes 01, Q2)

Seen in the image: a woman's tanned face at lower right, looking up; pale palm fronds and a white mountain above a small town with a church tower; 'MERANO' in large light-blue capitals on dark green; an ENIT emblem at lower left, an FS monogram emblem at lower right, the signature 'Lenhart' at top right

images.caption: Franz Lenhart, 1934. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, Hungarian National Museum via Europeana; the artwork is in copyright until 2062.

entries.creator: Franz Lenhart
entries.rights: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Hungarian National Museum, via Europeana)

entries.title: Merano
text: A tourist poster for Merano: a blossoming tree, the gorge of the Passer with its stone bridge, the state railways' “ITALIA” emblem. The date comes from the copy in the Touriseum. This is a small dealer's scan with a watermark.
facts: Tourist poster 'MERANO': Passer gorge, Steinerner Steg, blossoming tree; FS 'ITALIA' logo; printer Richter & C. Napoli; the Touriseum holds a copy dated 1935 (inv. 4090390) (manifest)
The date comes from the Touriseum copy (manifest; notes 01, Q1 #37, [DB✓])
The Commons source is 'unknown' and the scan carries a '© Tous droits réservés' watermark from a dealer site, which claims the photo, not the PD artwork; low-res, 361×500 (manifest)
Blossom branch as a Merano motif: Lenhart 1938–39, Borgoni 1935, the Barabino & Graeve Dirndl poster 1935 (notes 01, Q4, [DB✓, IMG✓])

Seen in the image: a blossoming tree fills the left foreground; behind it a gorge with an arched stone bridge, towers and terraced slopes under mountains; 'MERANO' in cream capitals at lower left; a circular FS monogram above 'ITALIA' and 'Richter & C. Napoli' at lower right; '© Tous droits réservés' in the bottom corner

entries.title: Ortisei – Val Gardena
text: Erwin Merlet's poster for Ortisei in the Val Gardena, 1935: an orange cable-car cabin, skiers, a smiling man in yellow. It was published in Bolzano by Amonn.

The province's image was mostly drawn locally and then made national through emblems, approval stamps and national printers. The small print here seems to record the ministry's approval of the sketch.
facts: Tourist poster 'ORTISEI – VAL Gardena': cable car, Sassolungo, skiers; imprint 'Edizione J. F. Amonn S.A. Bolzano' (manifest)
Commons source: artnet; low-res, 331×470 (manifest)
Erwin Merlet (Wien 1886 – Südtirol 1939): 'Colle Isarco' (ENIT/FS, 1939) [DB✓]; this 'Ortisei – Val Gardena' (1935, Edizione J. F. Amonn, Bolzano) [IMG✓] (notes 01, Q2)
The province's image was mostly made locally (Lenhart, Merlet, Tscholl, Bährendt, Fränzl) and then nationalised through ENIT/FS logos, approval stamps and national printers (notes 01, Q2, [INF])

Seen in the image: an orange cable-car cabin at upper left against a pale rock tower; skiers on snowfields below, a smiling man in a yellow cap and jacket at lower right; 'ORTISEI' in white capitals at top, 'VAL Gardena' at lower left; a line of small print under the imprint seems to read 'Bozzetto approvato dal Ministero per la Stampa e la Propaganda – Direzione Generale per il Turismo …' (low resolution)

images.caption: Erwin Merlet, 1935. Public domain. Wikimedia Commons (from artnet).

entries.rights: Public domain (author died more than 70 years ago)

entries.title: 700-166. Bolzano: Panorama verso le Dolomiti
text: A photographic postcard of 1940, “Bolzano: Panorama verso le Dolomiti”. Rows of large new blocks fill the valley floor in front of the old town. The new city, missing from every poster, is the foreground of a postcard.
Going by its series number it is very probably a card by the Bolzano publisher Fränzl.
facts: Real-photo postcard '700-166. BOLZANO: Panorama verso le DOLOMITI', with the new Gries/Neustadt blocks in the foreground (manifest)
The '700-' numbering matches Fränzl's series (700-64, 700-91, 700-181, 700-422), so it is very probably a Fränzl card (notes 01, Q5, [INF])
Division of labour between media: postcards and the press carried the new state's monuments and infrastructure, posters a timeless alpine Alto Adige (notes 01, Q4, [INF])

Seen in the image: a black-and-white view over orchards and villas to rows of large new blocks across the valley floor, the town beyond and a jagged snow-covered range on the horizon at upper left; caption '700-166. BOLZANO: Panorama verso le DOLOMITI' at lower left

images.caption: Unknown publisher (probably Fränzl), 1940. Public domain (PD-Italy). Wikimedia Commons.

entries.rights: Public domain (PD-Italy, simple photographs 20 years; PD-1996)

confidence.note: publisher not stated; Fränzl is an inference from the series number
